title: Should and ought to
summary: **Should** и **ought to** для советов и оценок, ожиданий («должно быть уже...»), упрёков с **should have + V3**, а также эмоциональное **should** и формальное **Should you need...**.
ru:
## Совет и оценка: should и ought to
Базовое значение вам знакомо: **should** — «следует», «стоило бы». Продвинутый уровень начинается с тонкостей. **Should** — самый частотный и универсальный способ дать совет или высказать мнение; **ought to** ощущается чуть более «объективным» (так положено, правильно с точки зрения морали или правил) и в США встречается реже:
> You **should** see a specialist about that cough. — Вам стоит показаться специалисту с этим кашлем.
> We **ought to** report this to the police. — Нам следует сообщить об этом в полицию.
Отрицание **shouldn't** обычное; **oughtn't to** — формально, по-британски, и звучит несколько книжно. В вопросах почти всегда используют **should**: **Should** I tell him? (а не ~~Ought I to tell him?~~, хотя грамматически возможно).

## Ожидание: «должно быть»
Когда мы считаем, что что-то вероятно (на основе расписания, опыта), используем **should / ought to**:
> The parcel **should** arrive tomorrow. — Посылка должна прийти завтра.
> Tom left an hour ago, so he **ought to be** home by now. — Том ушёл час назад, так что он уже должен быть дома.
Отличие от **must**: **must** говорит о выводе на основании фактов («должно быть, так и есть»), а **should** — об ожидании, которое может не оправдаться. Если вы не уверены в исходе вообще, скажите **may** или **might**.

## Should have + V3: упрёк, сожаление, ожидание
> You **should have booked** earlier. — Тебе следовало забронировать раньше (а ты не сделал).
> She **shouldn't have said** that. — Ей не следовало это говорить (но она сказала).
> The report **should have been** finished by Friday. — Отчёт должен был быть готов к пятнице.
Также: «по моим расчётам, это уже произошло»: Her plane **should have landed** by now.

## Should в формальной и эмоциональной речи
- **Should + подлежащее** вместо if в официальных условных предложениях:
> **Should you need** further help, please contact reception. — Если вам понадобится помощь, обращайтесь на ресепшн.
- **should** после слов эмоциональной оценки (surprised, odd, strange, a pity): It's odd that he **should** say that. — Странно, что он такое сказал.
- Риторический вопрос: **How should** I know? / **Why should** I apologise? — Откуда мне знать? / С какой стати мне извиняться?
- Британский формальный стиль: I **should** like to thank you. — Я хотел бы поблагодарить вас.

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~You should to go home.~~ → You **should go** home.
- ~~He should goes.~~ → He **should go**.
- ~~You should better rest.~~ → You **had better** rest. / You **should** rest.
- ~~You should have went.~~ → You should have **gone**.
en:
## Advice and opinion: should and ought to
You know the basic meaning: **should** = it is a good idea / the right thing to do. At a higher level the details matter. **Should** is the most common and flexible way to give advice or an opinion. **Ought to** feels slightly more 'objective' (it is right, morally or by the rules) and is less common in American English:
> You **should** see a specialist about that cough.
> We **ought to** report this to the police.
The negative **shouldn't** is normal. **Oughtn't to** is formal, mostly British and rather old-fashioned. In questions we normally use **should**: **Should** I tell him?

## Expectation
When something is probable (because of a timetable or experience) we use **should / ought to**:
> The parcel **should** arrive tomorrow.
> Tom left an hour ago, so he **ought to be** home by now.
**Must** is a conclusion based on facts; **should** is an expectation that may turn out wrong. If you are not really sure about the outcome, use may or might.

## Should have + past participle
> You **should have booked** earlier. (you did not)
> She **shouldn't have said** that. (she did)
> The report **should have been** finished by Friday.
Also: 'I expect it has happened': Her plane **should have landed** by now.

## Formal and emotional uses
- **Should + subject** instead of if:
> **Should you need** further help, please contact reception.
- **should** after expressions of surprise or emotion: It's odd that he **should** say that.
- Rhetorical questions: **How should** I know? / **Why should** I apologise?
- Formal British: I **should** like to thank you.

## Common mistakes
- ~~You should to go home.~~ → You **should go** home.
- ~~He should goes.~~ → He **should go**.
- ~~You should better rest.~~ → You **had better** rest.
- ~~You should have went.~~ → You should have **gone**.
structure:
## Формулы
| Значение | Форма | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| совет | should / ought to + V | You **should** sleep more. |
| отрицание | shouldn't / oughtn't to + V | You **shouldn't** worry. |
| ожидание, настоящее | should / ought to + be / V | He **should be** here soon. |
| ожидание, к моменту | should have + V3 | She **should have arrived**. |
| упрёк, сожаление | should have + V3 | I **should have called**. |
| упрёк в процессе | should have been + V-ing | You **should have been working**. |
| формальное if | **Should** + подлежащее + V | **Should** you need help, call us. |
| эмоция | that + подлежащее + **should** + V | It's odd that she **should** be late. |

## Сравнение: should, ought to, must, had better
| Форма | Оттенок | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| should | мнение, совет, универсально | You should apologise. |
| ought to | «так правильно», чуть более объективно | We ought to help them. |
| must | сильное обязательство, твёрдый вывод | You must apologise. |
| had better | совет с угрозой последствий | You'd better apologise, or else. |

## Отрицание и вопрос
> You **should not** (shouldn't) / **ought not to** (oughtn't to) do it.
> **Should** we leave now? — Yes, we **should**. / No, we **shouldn't**.
> Why **shouldn't** I? — С какой стати мне нельзя?

exercises.title: Should / ought to
exercises.instruction: Вставьте нужную форму should или ought to (с have, если нужно). Допустимые варианты засчитываются.

items.text: You {{should|ought to}} see a specialist about that cough.
The meeting {{should|ought to}} be over by now — it started at nine.
You {{shouldn't have|should not have|oughtn't to have|ought not to have}} told her the secret; now everybody knows.
We {{should have|ought to have}} booked earlier; all the hotels are full now.
{{Should}} you need any assistance, please contact reception.
It's odd that she {{should}} be so upset about such a small thing.
How {{should|would}} I know where he is?

exercises.title: Should have + причастие
exercises.instruction: Вставьте нужную форму глагола в скобках (причастие или -ing).

items.text: We should have {{left}} earlier; now we'll miss the train.
She shouldn't have {{spoken}} to him like that.
You ought to have {{told}} me about the problem sooner.
He should have {{arrived}} an hour ago. I wonder what has happened.
They should have been {{doing}} their homework instead of watching TV.
The report should {{have been}} finished by Friday, but it wasn't.
He ought not to have {{driven}} after drinking at the party.

items.q: You look exhausted. You ___ a holiday.
Tom left an hour ago, so he ___ home by now.
I'm sorry, I ___ so rude to you yesterday.
___ you have any problems, call our helpline.
'Why ___ I apologise? It wasn't my fault.'
items.why: Риторический вопрос: **Why should I...?** — «С какой стати?».

items.q: It's astonishing that he ___ even think of such a thing.
Her flight left at nine, so she ___ landed by now.
items.why: Ожидание, что действие уже произошло → **should have + V3**.

items.q: Какое предложение — упрёк за прошлое действие?

options: Посылка обязана прийти завтра, иначе штраф.
Should you require further information, please let us know.
If you need more information, tell us.
If you want more information, just ask.
Вам следовало работать (а вы не работали).
items.why: **should have been + -ing** — упрёк: нужно было делать, но не делали.

exercises.title: Перепишите с should / ought to
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение, используя should или ought to. Начало дано.

items.prompt: It was a mistake not to book earlier. → We ...
answers: We ought to have booked earlier.

items.prompt: It's a bad idea to drive so fast. → You ...
answers: You should not drive so fast.
You ought not to drive so fast.
You oughtn't to drive so fast.

items.prompt: I expect the delivery will arrive on Thursday. → The delivery ...
answers: The delivery should arrive on Thursday.
The delivery ought to arrive on Thursday.

items.prompt: If you need help, call me. (formal inversion) → Should ...
answers: Should you need help, call me.
Should you need help, please call me.
Should you need any help, call me.
Should you need any help, please call me.

items.prompt: It was wrong of him to leave so early. → He ...
answers: He shouldn't have left so early.
He should not have left so early.
He oughtn't to have left so early.
He ought not to have left so early.

items.prompt: You didn't lock the door, and that was a mistake. → You ...
answers: You should have locked the door.
You ought to have locked the door.

exercises.title: Напишите о себе
exercises.instruction: Ответьте полными предложениями, используя should, ought to или should have.

items.prompt: Give advice to someone who wants to learn a language quickly.
items.sample: You should speak every day and shouldn't be afraid of mistakes.

items.prompt: Write about something you should have done differently last year.
items.sample: I should have started saving money earlier.

items.prompt: What should be happening in your city but isn't?
items.sample: The new metro line should be open by now, but it isn't.

items.prompt: Write about a rule people ought to follow more carefully.
items.sample: Drivers ought to slow down near schools.

items.prompt: Write a formal sentence for a hotel notice using 'Should you ...'.
items.sample: Should you require anything during your stay, please call reception.

items.prompt: What should a new employee know on the first day at work?
items.sample: A new employee should ask questions and shouldn't be afraid to make mistakes.
